title: Regulatory Frameworks - EU, US, UK, Korea

questions.question: When did the EU AI Act enter into force, and what category applied first?
options: August 2024; prohibited practices and AI literacy applied 2 February 2025
August 2026; only GPAI applied at force-date
August 2025; all categories applied at once
January 2024; high-risk systems applied that day
questions.explanation: The AI Act entered into force 1 August 2024, but its obligations apply on a staggered timeline: prohibited practices and AI literacy requirements were the first category to apply, from 2 February 2025.

questions.question: What is the maximum monetary penalty under the EU AI Act, and which violations trigger it?
options: Up to 35M EUR or 7% of worldwide annual turnover, for violations of prohibited AI practices (Article 5)
Up to 15M EUR or 3% of worldwide annual turnover, for non-compliance with other obligations under the Act
Up to 7.5M EUR or 1% of worldwide annual turnover, for supplying incorrect information to authorities
Unlimited, since the AI Act sets no cap on fines
questions.explanation: Article 99(3) sets the highest penalty tier at up to 35M EUR or 7% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, for violations of the prohibited practices in Article 5. Lower tiers apply to other violations: 15M EUR / 3% under Article 99(4) for other non-compliance, and 7.5M EUR / 1% under Article 99(5) for supplying incorrect information to authorities.

questions.question: Which three chapters make up the GPAI Code of Practice (10 July 2025)?
options: Training, Inference, Deployment
Capability, Control, Compliance
Privacy, Bias, Watermarking
Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security
questions.explanation: The GPAI Code of Practice (10 July 2025) has three chapters: Transparency (binding all GPAI providers), Copyright (all GPAI providers), and Safety and Security (binding only systemic-risk GPAI providers, an estimated 5-15 companies).

questions.question: What does the February 2025 UK AISI rebrand to 'AI Security Institute' signal?
options: A narrower scope focused on frontier-capability security, dropping algorithmic bias and free-speech framings
Merger with the EU AI Office
Closure of UK frontier evaluation
Expansion into algorithmic bias
questions.explanation: The rebrand from 'AI Safety Institute' to 'AI Security Institute' narrows the body's scope: it drops the earlier algorithmic-bias and free-speech framings and focuses on frontier-capability security, while continuing to run its open-sourced Inspect evaluation tool.

questions.question: What does the US CAISI rebrand (June 2025) signal in policy direction?
options: Merger with FDA
Stricter pre-deployment safety evaluation
A shift toward 'pro-growth AI policies,' with emphasis on standards and innovation support and reduced emphasis on pre-deployment evaluation
Mandatory open-source release of frontier models
questions.explanation: The Trump administration renamed NIST's AI Safety Institute to the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) in June 2025, shifting toward 'pro-growth AI policies' with more emphasis on standards and innovation support and less on pre-deployment evaluation, acting as a domestic counterweight to the EU AI Act's stricter posture.

questions.question: What is the headline obligation in Korea's AI Framework Act (effective January 2026)?
options: Identical adoption of the EU AI Act
Mandatory open-weights for all generative models
Total prohibition of foreign AI providers
Article 12 establishes an AISI under MSIT and mandates local representatives, risk assessment, and safety measures for high-impact and generative AI
questions.explanation: Korea's AI Framework Act, effective January 2026, establishes an AI Safety Institute under the Ministry of Science and ICT (Article 12) and requires local representatives for foreign AI companies, risk assessment for high-impact systems, and safety measures for generative and high-impact AI.
